key_insight: MoRight factorizes motion and viewpoint control while enforcing motion causality so user-specified actions produce physically coherent reactions from other objects across arbitrary camera views.
problem_solved: Existing video generation methods conflate camera and object motion and fail to produce causal responses—resulting in unrealistic or pixel-shifted reactions when users try to control object actions or change viewpoints.
method: Factorized control: separate latent controls for object motion and camera viewpoint so each can be adjusted independently.
Interaction-aware dynamics: a module that predicts object-state changes and enforces causal responses of other objects rather than mere pixel displacement.
View-consistent synthesis: a rendering/decoding component that produces physically plausible frames under freely chosen viewpoints while respecting the predicted dynamics.
impact: Enables intuitive, reliable motion-conditioned video synthesis useful for interactive content creation, realistic simulation for robotics, and data augmentation where controllable, causally consistent scene dynamics across viewpoints are required.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram showing factorization: separate object-motion and camera-view branches feeding a shared renderer.
Before/after comparatives: entangled pixel-shift output vs. MoRight's causally consistent reaction sequences.
Interaction graph overlaid on frames: arrows showing predicted causal influence between objects when one is controlled.
Viewpoint sweep: same controlled action rendered from multiple camera angles demonstrating view consistency.
paper_authors: Shaowei Liu, Xuanchi Ren, Tianchang Shen, Huan Ling, Saurabh Gupta
